title: finding(fields): `signature` is a spec STRING_VALUE_TYPES member but renders through ImageCellRenderer, so `{}` draws "No value" where its own value class prints `[Object]`
body: Found while closing the `{}` column of the cell-renderer census (objectui#8596), by rendering all 53 registered field types through `getCellRenderer` against `[]`, `{}`, `''` and `null` on `4eb665bcf`. Out of that card's scope, filed rather than swept. ## What was measured `signature` holding `{}` renders the shared "No value" affordance: ```html - ``` `text` — and every other member of the same spec value class — renders `[Object]` for the same input. ## Why that is a divergence and not a preference `@objectstack/spec` v17.3.0 `src/data/field-value.zod.ts` places `signature` in **`STRING_VALUE_TYPES`** ("Value is a plain string"; `valueSchemaFor` returns `z.string()`), alongside `text` / `textarea` / `email` / `url` / `phone` / `color` / `markdown` / `html` / `richtext` / `code` / `qrcode`. objectui#8580 ruled `{}` for that class and objectui#8596 applied the same ruling to the rest of it: the record IS storing something, so "No value" is false of it, and the cell prints the family's existing coercion (`coerceToSafeValue`, byte-equal to what `text` prints). After objectui#8596 every `STRING_VALUE_TYPES` member prints `[Object]` for `{}` — except `signature`. The cause is the renderer map, not the ruling: `signature` resolves to `ImageCellRenderer` (`getCellRenderer`'s `standardMap` maps `image`, `avatar` and `signature` to it), and that renderer normalises through `readFileValues(...).filter((v) => v.url)` — the media rule, where `url` is the spec's one required member. `image` and `avatar` are genuinely `FILE_REFERENCE_TYPES`, so the media rule is right for them; `signature` is not in that set. ## The question this needs a ruling on Which side moves: - **A.** `signature` is a string in the spec, so its cell should answer `{}` like `text` does. That means the string case cannot go through the media rule, and `SignatureCellRenderer` (or a string arm inside `ImageCellRenderer`) becomes a distinct thing. - **B.** A signature is stored as an image in practice and the spec's classification is the thing that is off, in which case the fix is in `@objectstack/spec`, not here (AGENTS.md #0.1: fix the contract, not the renderer). Not guessed here. Whichever way it goes, the answer belongs in one place and both `image` and `signature` should then be able to state it. ## Scope note Only the `{}` input diverges. `null`, `''` and `[]` all render the affordance on both sides, and a populated signature (`{ url: ... }`) renders its thumbnail — unchanged and unaffected. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_
